one_month_reasoning: Revised. In 2026 Hudbay has reported about two weeks earlier than in 2025 (Q1 on Apr 30/May 1, Q2 on Jul 29, versus May 13 and Aug 13 in 2025), and aggregators list Q3 for Oct 28, so I now put roughly a 65% chance on Q3 results landing inside the window (the date is not confirmed; the call notice normally comes about three weeks ahead). Consensus is $0.36-0.37 against a Q2 actual of $0.28. That bar is high but reachable: Q3 copper averaged about the Q2 level or above, about 10kt of Peru concentrate delayed from Q2 was shipped in July so Q3 sales should catch up, and BC throughput rose as guided. Gold is lower ($4,187 now against a $4,312 Q2 realized price). Other items in the window: the fresh Snow Lake mine-plan upgrade (Sep 28; reserve life to 2043, 185koz/yr gold at $821/oz cash cost) and the Oct-2 open about 4% higher; LME Week in mid-October (2027 TC/RC talks, spot TCs deeply negative, which favours concentrate sellers); Freeport and Antofagasta Q3 reports in late October; and Section 232 refined-copper tariff headlines (a 15% tariff from 1 Jan 2027 is still undecided). I use a lognormal with a median of $26.4, slightly above spot, and monthly sigma of 19% (63%/3.5 = 18%, widened slightly for a likely earnings print). Oct 31 is a Saturday, so the effective mark is the Oct 30 close.

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA ($1.55B on guided volumes at a haircut deck x 7.5x, about $20M attributable net debt, 444.1M shares -> $26.1, weight 0.35), an asset SOTP/NAV at a $5.25/lb long-term copper deck (~$11.0B -> $24.7, weight 0.45), and 2027E P/E ($1.55 x 15x -> $23.3, weight 0.2) = $24.9, rounded to $25. At a spot deck ($6.50 Cu, $4,190 Au) the same methods give about $30.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E adj. EBITDA $1.55B x 7.5x = EV $11.6B; less attributable net debt $0.02B; / 444.1M shares = $26.1

inputs_detail.derivation: Guidance midpoint less about 6% for execution risk on the Copper Mountain ramp (BC guided 50-70kt versus 25-35kt in 2026) and Constancia pebble-crusher throughput. Gold is about 235koz against a 213-269koz guide.

H1 2026 annualised is $1.49B on about 112kt Cu, at a realised ~$5.97/lb Cu and ~$4,390/oz Au. Add about 40kt of incremental copper at about a $3.0/lb incremental margin (+$265M). Subtract the copper deck move to $5.75/lb, about 12% below the ~$6.50 spot (-$55M), the gold deck move to $3,900 from ~$4,390 on about 200koz (-$100M), and about $50M of cost inflation. That gives $1.55B. At a spot deck it is about $1.85B.

Capstone trades at about 5.5x CY26 and 6.4x LTM. HBM gets a premium of about 1.5-2x because Arizona (Copper World 70% plus Cactus, about $2.9B of growth value) is not in EBITDA, and for its net-cash balance sheet and gold by-product. Unchanged from round 1.

inputs_detail.value: ~$20M (reported net debt -$80.5M plus 30% of $334.5M Copper World LLC cash)
inputs_detail.derivation: Reported net cash is $80.5M. 30% of the ring-fenced Copper World cash belongs to Mitsubishi, which leaves about $20M of attributable net debt.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Peru/Constancia $3.3B + Manitoba/Snow Lake $3.0B + BC/Copper Mountain (100%) $2.0B + Copper World 70% $1.7B + Cactus $1.2B + Mason/exploration $0.4B - corporate G&A/closure $0.6B - attributable net debt $0.02B = ~$11.0B / 444.1M = $24.7

inputs_detail.derivation: PFS Phase I after-tax NPV8 is $1.1B at $3.75/lb and $1.7B at $4.25 (+$0.6B per +$0.50/lb). At $5.25 that is about $2.9B at 100%. I subtract about $0.5B because DFS capex will come in above the PFS (inflation and mill scope, per the Q2 MD&A), giving about $2.4B. 70% is $1.7B. That sits above the floor of about $1.4B for 70% implied by Mitsubishi paying $600M for 30%.
Shares issued were worth $1,135.6M (Q2 FS note 4), plus a modest mark-up for higher copper since the deal.
185koz/yr of gold over 2026-30 at $1,379/oz sustaining cost. At a $3,800 long-term gold price that is about $450M/yr pre-tax and about $330M after tax, with reserve life to 2043, discounted at 8%.
100% owned since Apr 2025. Guided 50-70kt Cu in 2027 and about 57.5kt average with mine life to 2045, but a higher-cost operation. Up from $1.6B in round 1 on the guided volumes.
About 87.5-90kt Cu/yr to 2040 at $5.25/lb long term, about 6x unlevered FCF. Unchanged from round 1.
Paid into the Copper World JV for Mitsubishi's 30%. Adding it on top of a 70% project value double-counts.
The Q3 consensus annualised is about $1.48 at near-spot prices. Guided volume growth of about +25% adds earnings, but my haircut deck ($5.75 Cu, $3,900 Au) takes most of it back, net about +5%.
A mid-cycle multiple for a mid-cap copper-gold producer, consistent with the peer EV/EBITDA of about 5.5-6.5x plus HBM's growth premium.

bear.story: Copper corrects to about $4.75-5.0/lb as 962kt of visible exchange stocks and an unwind of the US tariff stockpile outweigh the mine-supply deficit, and gold falls to about $3,500. 2027 EBITDA is about $1.1B even with part of the volume growth, at about 6x, and Arizona gets only half credit. A disappointing Copper World DFS capex figure or Peru unrest under the Fujimori government adds to the de-rating.

base.story: Copper holds around $5.75-6.5/lb on supply problems (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Chile) and negative TCs. Hudbay delivers most of the guided 2027 copper step-up (around 150-160kt), so 2027-28 EBITDA is about $1.7B. Copper World is sanctioned around year-end 2026 with Mitsubishi funding 30%, and Snow Lake runs at about 185koz. At about 7x EBITDA plus Arizona, the stock moves into the high $20s.

bull.story: Copper rises to $7+/lb as the deficit deepens (UBS $15,000/t; Citi $15-17k), gold recovers above $4.5k, and Copper Mountain ramps cleanly to the top of its 50-70kt range. EBITDA heads toward $2.2B, and the Copper World sanction re-rates HBM as a US copper developer. The stock reaches the top of sell-side targets and beyond.

thesis_break_reason: About -37%, still above the $14.34 52-week low. At $16.5 the market cap of about $7.3B is under 5x my haircut-deck 2027E EBITDA of $1.55B and gives almost no credit for Copper World (Mitsubishi implies at least about $1.4B for 70%) or Cactus (about $1.14B paid in stock). Trading there would most likely mean copper had broken durably below about $4.75/lb, the guided 2027 volume step-up was failing (a Copper Mountain ramp problem), a Copper World capex or funding shock was forcing equity issuance, or there was a Constancia/Peru disruption, rather than ordinary 60% vol noise. Lowered from $17 because the confirmed volume growth gives more fundamental support.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's filing checks corrected three of my inputs, and I verified each one in the primary 6-Ks. (1) Volumes: 2027 copper is guided at 140-184kt versus 110-138kt in 2026 (BC 50-70kt versus 25-35kt, Peru 80-100kt), not 'flat to lower'. Rebuilt from H1 2026 EBITDA of $743M (annualised $1.49B) with the volume step-up on a deck about 12% below spot, 2027E EBITDA is about $1.55B, up from $1.35B, and the EV/EBITDA leg rises from $23.0 to $26.1. (2) The Copper World PFS sensitivity is +$0.6B per +$0.50/lb, not +$1.1B. My 70% value falls from $2.6B to $1.7B, and I remove the $180M Mitsubishi contribution as a double count. Partly offsetting this, BC is worth more on guided volumes, Snow Lake more after the Sep 28 mine-plan upgrade, and I now use the reported 444.1M shares and about $20M of attributable net debt. Net, the SOTP falls from $28.0 to $24.7. (3) I added a P/E leg on the $0.37 Q3 consensus ($23.3). My blended fair value is $25.0, about $1.5 below my round-1 figure and $2 below the supervisor's $27. I disagree with the supervisor's level mainly on deck and Copper World capex: I value at $5.75 near-term and $5.25 long-term copper and haircut Copper World for DFS capex inflation. At spot metals the same build gives about $30. My industry-lane evidence is unchanged: record-negative TCs and mine-supply losses support prices; doubled visible inventories and the Section 232 stockpile overhang are the main downside. For the 12-month ladder, fair value matters less than the metals path, and the confirmed volume growth gives operating leverage in the base case, so I raised the base scenario to $28 (bear $18 / bull $40 at 25/50/25, expected value about $28.5). The ladder is a lognormal mixture with within-case sigma of about 0.27-0.33 and slightly fattened tails. The median is about $27.6, P(>= $26) = 0.57 versus 0.55 in round 1, and the downside tail is a bit thinner because volume growth cushions a metals pullback. For the 1-month ladder, Q3 is now probably inside the window, so the median is slightly above spot and the spread slightly wider. Extra research was limited to the March 2026 outlook 6-K, the Q2 MD&A, the Sep 28 Snow Lake 6-K and one tariff-status search.
